div.div:
NON-OVERLAP VERIFICATION (PROVED)
• Centers vs AWS Supernet: 10.47.255.255 < 10.80.0.0 [PASS]
• AWS Supernet vs Azure: 10.87.255.255 < 10.88.0.0 [PASS]
• AWS Environments: 10.80.255.255 < 10.81.0.0 < 10.82.0.0 [PASS]
• Prefix Boundary Alignment:
* /13 on mod-8 octet (40, 80, 88)
* /14 on mod-4 octet (84)
* /22 on mod-4 octet (all tier subnets: 0, 4, 8, 12, ...)
* /28 on mod-16 octet (transit subnets: 0, 16, 32, 48)
Verified with Python ipaddress module and exact prefix boundaries.

div.div: Case Statement Technical Constraint: "El patrón de red y de ingesta escala de 200 a 1.000 fincas sin rediseñar el direccionamiento ni el punto de ingesta" (Point 3 & Part A: scales from 200 to 1,000 farms without redesigning addressing or the ingestion point; ASM-032, ASM-036)

box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #2d3748;
display: inline-block; font-size: 13.5px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#2d3748, #b7bfce); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
1. Architectural Scalability: Identity, Not IP
• Zero Cloud Private IP Consumption: Farms DO NOT receive private cloud IP addresses (ASM-032).
• Public Cellular Bearer: Nodes publish over cellular data (or satellite IP bearer) to the regional public endpoint (AWS IoT Core).
• Authentication by Identity: Devices authenticate via mutual TLS with X.509 certificates and FarmId identities, not IP addresses.
• Linear Expansion: Scaling from 200 to 1,000 farms adds 800 device identities to the existing endpoint.
• Zero Network Topology Changes: ZERO subnet, route table, interface endpoint, or CIDR block changes required.
• Store-and-Forward: Local non-volatile encrypted outbox buffers up to 24 hours of readings when signal is absent.
• Transporters & Drones: Transporter phones and drone uploads over public cellular operate on the same identity principle.

div.div:
2. Ingestion Load Scaling (5x Volume)
• Pilot Baseline Load at 200 Farms (Case Statement Part A):
* Cultivation: 200 farms x 6 readings/day = 1,200 readings/day
* Active drying (harvest): 100 farms x 24 readings/day = 2,400 readings/day
* Total pilot daily load: 3,600 readings/day (~0.04 readings/sec average)
• Expanded Load at 1,000 Farms (ASM-036):
* Cultivation: 1,000 farms x 6 readings/day = 6,000 readings/day
* Active drying (harvest): 500 farms x 24 readings/day = 12,000 readings/day
* Total expanded load: 18,000 readings/day (~0.21 readings/sec average)
• Capacity Impact: 0.21 readings/second is trivial for managed AWS IoT Core data plane. Ingestion capacity scales elastically without any network redesign.

div.div:
3. Pessimistic Address Headroom Analysis (telemetry_ingress)
Even under a deliberately pessimistic hypothetical bound where every farm consumed one private VPC IP:
• Usable addresses in telemetry_ingress active AZ slots: 3 x 1,019 = 3,057 usable IPs
• 200 farms consumption: 200 IPs (6.5% of tier capacity) -> 2,857 free IPs
• 1,000 farms consumption: 1,000 IPs (32.7% of tier capacity) -> 2,057 free IPs
• Worst-case single AZ concentration: 1,000 farms fits within ONE single /22 slot (1,019 usable IPs)!
• Additional tier headroom without readdressing:
* az4 slot reserved: 1,019 additional IPs
* 8 reserved tier blocks (10.E.112.0 to 10.E.239.255): 32,768 IPs per environment
• Collection Centers: 10.40.0.0/13 summary route already encompasses fourth department (10.44.0.0/16)
